description: The graph illustrates the relationship between accuracy and population frequency for two metrics—initial accuracy and final accuracy—across a range of population frequencies scaled by 10^4. The x-axis, labeled "pop frequency (x10^4)", spans from approximately 1 to 17, with tick marks at intervals of 2, representing the frequency of population samples. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy", ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals, indicating the performance metric being measured. The "Initial Accuracy" is represented by a green line with square markers, showing a general upward trend from an initial value of approximately 0.4 at a population frequency of 1 to a peak of about 0.9 at a frequency of 11, followed by a slight decline to around 0.85 at 17. The "Final Accuracy" is depicted by a blue dashed line with circular markers, which begins at approximately 0.7 at a frequency of 1, fluctuates with a peak near 0.9 at a frequency of 13, and ends at about 0.95 at a frequency of 17. Both lines exhibit variability, with error bars indicating the uncertainty in the measurements, particularly noticeable at higher frequencies.
